Chapter 9. Differential Expression

Source: vignettes/articles/09-Differential-Expression.Rmd
09-Differential-Expression.Rmd

Correcting counts and then running a standard test is one way to deal with ambient RNA in differential expression. Decant offers a second way: ambient_de() keeps the raw counts and models each sample’s soup inside the test.

9.1 The problem

Suppose disease samples carry more ambient RNA than control samples, and that ambient RNA is rich in the disease genes of an abundant cell type, A. A pseudobulk test on a rare cell type, R, sees those genes rise in R’s disease samples and reports them as differentially expressed in R. They are not. Their rise is entirely due to the soup.

9.2 The model

For each gene g and sample s, ambient_de() fits

counts[g, s]  ~  NegativeBinomial( native expression[g, s]  +  rho[s] × total[s] × soup[g, s] )
  • The native expression term depends on the design (for example control versus disease) and is what is tested.
  • The ambient term is measured: soup from the sample’s own empty droplets and rho estimated from the data. It is added to the mean, not subtracted from the counts, and its uncertainty is carried into the test.
  • The test is a quasi-likelihood F-test, as in edgeR.

9.3 Example 

library(Decant)
st <- simulate_ambient_study(seed = 3, G = 600, n_cells = 500)
table(st$cond)
#>
#> ctrl  dis
#>    6    6
  • simulate_ambient_study() creates 6 control and 6 disease samples. Cell type A is abundant and has 80 disease genes; cell type R is rare and has 40 of its own. Disease samples carry more ambient RNA than controls.

Pseudobulk the cell type of interest 

is_R <- st$label == "R"
samples <- sort(unique(st$sample))
Y <- vapply(samples, function(s)
  rowSums(st$X[, is_R & st$sample == s, drop = FALSE]), numeric(nrow(st$X)))
rownames(Y) <- rownames(st$X)
dim(Y)
#> [1] 600  12
  • is_R selects the cells of the rare type.
  • vapply() sums those cells’ counts within each sample, giving one column per sample: the pseudobulk matrix Y, genes × samples.

Run the test 

design <- model.matrix(~ cond, data = data.frame(cond = st$cond))
res <- ambient_de(Y, st$empties, design)
head(res[, c("gene", "logFC", "FDR", "ambient_frac", "naive_FDR", "ambient_driven")], 3)
#>     gene    logFC          FDR ambient_frac    naive_FDR ambient_driven
#> 117 g218 1.461912 1.129595e-07   0.02752255 3.990660e-07          FALSE
#> 173 g309 1.226158 2.978136e-07   0.01134339 1.797587e-06          FALSE
#> 189 g338 1.183623 4.248957e-06   0.01707194 9.899770e-06          FALSE
  • design is a standard model matrix with one row per sample. The last column (conddis, disease versus control) is tested by default.
  • st$empties is a list of empty-droplet matrices, one per sample, in the same order as the columns of Y.
  • Results are ordered by p-value. The key columns are:
Column Meaning
logFC log2 fold change of native expression
PValue, FDR Contamination-aware p-value and false discovery rate
ambient_frac Average share of the gene’s counts that are ambient
naive_FDR FDR of a standard edgeR test on the same pseudobulk
ambient_driven TRUE if the standard test calls the gene and the contamination-aware test does not

Genes explained by the soup 

sum(res$ambient_driven)
#> [1] 12
  • Twelve genes would be reported by a standard pipeline but are explained by differences in the soup between conditions. These are the calls ambient_de() protects you from.

Per-sample estimates 

head(attr(res, "samples"), 3)
#>   sample ambient_frac ambient_frac_imputed soup_umis norm_factor
#> 1      1   0.05692409                FALSE     49848   0.9663427
#> 2      2   0.05808700                FALSE     49966   1.0214589
#> 3      3   0.04450122                FALSE     50234   0.9746253
  • ambient_frac is the estimated ambient fraction of the cell type in each sample, and soup_umis the number of UMIs the sample’s soup rests on.
  • ambient_frac_imputed is TRUE for a sample whose own estimate was implausible (above max_rho) and was replaced by the median of the others (see 9.6).

9.4 From a Seurat object 

# Requires your own data
res <- DecantDE(obj, cell_type = "Microglia", sample_col = "donor",
                formula = ~ diagnosis, raw = raw_paths_by_donor)
subset(res, ambient_driven)
  • DecantDE() builds the pseudobulk, reads each sample’s empty droplets and calls ambient_de().
  • cell_type is the identity to test (Idents(obj) by default, or a column given in celltype_col).
  • sample_col names the sample of each cell; formula is the sample-level design. Every variable in formula must be constant within a sample.
  • raw is a named list with one raw matrix or Cell Ranger path per sample.

9.5 Useful options

Argument Default Purpose
coef last column Design column to test
robust TRUE Down-weight outlier samples gene by gene; important in large cohorts
lfc 0 Test against a minimum fold change, for example log2(1.1)
max_ambient_frac 0.75 Skip genes whose counts are mostly ambient; they are listed in attr(res, "ambient_dominated")
naive TRUE Also run the standard test, to fill naive_FDR and ambient_driven
joint_rho TRUE Refine each sample’s ambient fraction on genes absent from all samples pooled. Leave it on: without it, the ambient fraction of a single cell type can be wildly wrong
max_rho 0.5 A sample whose ambient fraction comes out above this takes the median of the other samples, with a warning
dispersion "trended" NB dispersion in the fit. "tagwise" was the earlier default and is not calibrated on real data (9.6)

9.6 Limits

  • ambient_de() is experimental. With condition labels shuffled between donors, so that there is nothing to find, on three real datasets (two brain, one pancreas; 168 tests) it reported a gene in 20 tests, never more than 9 genes; naive edgeR in 8. Earlier versions did far worse (up to 2,300 genes) and analyses made with them should be rerun. That it removes ambient-driven hits a standard test reports is shown only in simulation; a pre-registered real-data test was null, because the standard test found none. Report its hits together with a standard pseudobulk test, and check your own data the same way: shuffle the condition labels between samples and count the hits.
  • If ambient_de() warns that a sample’s ambient fraction is implausible, that sample’s pseudobulk looks too much like the soup to measure its contamination (often a cell type close to the dominant one, or mislabelled cells). Its value is replaced by the median of the others. If most samples are flagged, the results for that cell type are unreliable.
  • With very few empty droplets per sample (a few hundred), the soup is uncertain and some leakage returns.
  • With three samples per group, power is lower than with six.
  • Correcting counts with a good tool and then testing performs similarly on the same simulations; ambient_de() has the advantage when the design includes covariates such as batch.
